internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: The root contributes the notion of IMMINENT TEMPORAL DRAWING-NEAR: an appointed event pressing close / becoming at-hand in time. The invariant is not mere spatial or generic nearness but the impending, urgent approach of a fixed moment that is on the verge of arriving.
internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Only two verses carry the root, and one of them holds two of the three occurrences, which lets internal evidence arbitrate cleanly. In 53:57 the finite verb and the participle stand side by side: أَزِفَتِ ٱلْـَٔازِفَةُ — "the Āzifah has drawn near." The verb أَزِفَتْ (form I perfect) supplies the surface-explicit predicate "has drawn near / become imminent," and its subject ٱلْآزِفَةُ is the active participle from the same root used substantively as an epithet ("the Approaching / Impending one"). The fact that the root is predicated of its own participle — "the Approaching has approached" — shows the live charge is the ACT of temporal approach, not an emptied label. In 40:18, يَوْمَ ٱلْآزِفَةِ ("the Day of the Āzifah") uses the same participle as a name for the Day of Judgment; the continuation إِذِ ٱلْقُلُوبُ لَدَى ٱلْحَنَاجِرِ (hearts reaching the throats) frames it as an impending, pressing crisis. Across all three, subtracting the eschatological referent (the Hour/Day) leaves the same residue: something is on the point of arriving, temporally at hand.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: (a) FORM: form I perfect verb أَزِفَتْ = "drew near / became imminent" (53:57:1:1); active participle آزِفَة = "the one drawing near" used substantively (53:57:2:2 and 40:18:3:2). The participle nominalizes the verbal event into an agent-epithet. (b) CONSTRUCTION: intransitive throughout; no preposition supplies a directional or binding vector — the approach is inherent to the verb, subject-internal. In 40:18 the genitive iḍāfa يَوْمَ ٱلْآزِفَةِ ("Day of the Approaching") adds a temporal-container frame but does not alter the root sense. (c) PARTICIPANTS: subject is always the eschatological event (the Hour / the Day). (d) CONTEXT: uniformly eschatological/warning. After subtracting (a)-(d), the residue left in every case is pure temporal imminence: "on the verge of arrival."
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: The hardest case is 40:18:3:2, يَوْمَ ٱلْآزِفَةِ, where ٱلْآزِفَة functions as a fixed proper-name epithet for the Day of Judgment. One could argue the root here has bleached into a mere label ("the Hour"), losing the "approaching" content. It reconciles decisively via internal evidence: 53:57 predicates the verb أَزِفَتْ ("has drawn near") OF this very same participle ٱلْآزِفَةُ. That predication would be tautological/vacuous if the participle meant only "the Hour"; it is coherent only if the participle still carries "the Approaching one." So the naming use in 40:18 is a transparent derivation from the live sense of temporal approach, not a break from it.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: The strongest alternative is that the root simply denotes "the Hour / the eschatological event" as a bare designator, with no active "approach" content. Internal evidence arbitrates against it: in 53:57 the root's own verb أَزِفَتْ is predicated of the root's own participle ٱلْآزِفَةُ. If the root meant merely "the Hour," the sentence would say "the Hour hour-ed," which is empty; the sentence is informative only if the verb contributes "drew near / became imminent." Therefore the imminence-of-approach reading is required and the bare-designator reading fails. A second alternative — generic "nearness" (proximity in general) — is ruled out because every occurrence is temporal (an event about to arrive), never spatial or relational.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Nearest semantic neighbors: q-r-b (qaruba, "to be near" — broad, covers spatial, relational, and temporal nearness, and is stative), and d-n-w (danā, "to draw near / come close" — general approach, including spatial, e.g. 53:8). Azf is narrower than both: it denotes specifically the IMMINENT approach of an appointed moment in TIME, with a connotation of pressing urgency (the moment is virtually upon one). Where qaruba/danā can describe any degree or kind of nearness, Azf in this data is exclusively the impending arrival of a fixed temporal event. Falsifiability condition: if a confirmed occurrence used the root for spatial approach, for stable/static nearness, or for anything other than an impending temporal arrival, the "imminent temporal drawing-near" residue would be falsified.
internal_discovery.rationale: A single non-empty contribution — imminent temporal drawing-near — is recoverable in all three occurrences without forcing. The direction is determinate (approach toward arrival, not stative nearness) and surface-explicit: the form I verb أَزِفَتْ overtly means "has drawn near," and the participle آزِفَة is transparently "the approaching one." The two form-families (verb, participle) sit together in 53:57, where the verb is predicated of the participle, giving an internal near-proof that the participle-name preserves the verbal "approach" sense; this same participle is the label in 40:18, so unity holds across every occurrence. Distinctness from q-r-b and d-n-w is clear because the data confines Azf to impending temporal arrival. The only caution is the small, tightly clustered corpus (two of three in one verse), but the verb+participle co-predication makes the sense sharply determinate rather than inferential, so STRONG is warranted. No occurrence is left unreconciled; inconsistent_refs is empty.

adversarial_verification.notes: Tried hard to refute across all 3 occurrences (2 verses); found no genuine failing occurrence. ANCHOR (53:57): the verb أَزِفَتْ ('has drawn near', form I perfect) is a surface-explicit predicate of imminent temporal approach and is predicated of its own cognate participle ٱلْآزِفَةُ — 'the Approaching has approached'. This decisively proves the root is a LIVE act of temporal drawing-near, not an emptied label, and cannot be reduced to the eschatological referent. HARDEST CASE (40:18): يَوْمَ ٱلْآزِفَةِ uses the participle as a bare name for the Day, which a skeptic could argue empties the root into a label with imminence supplied by the referent. Rejected because (a) 53:57 already proves the root live, and (b) the context إِذِ ٱلْقُلُوبُ لَدَى ٱلْحَنَاجِرِ frames a pressing, impending crisis that confirms rather than empties the imminence charge. HOMONYMY PROBE: classical أزف also carries senses of haste (عجل) and straitness/distress (ضاق); I checked whether 40:18's distress context forces a 'distressing one' reading (potential split), but these senses are facets of urgent/pressing approach and reinforce the invariant — no Quranic occurrence forces a non-temporal reading. NEIGHBOR CONTRAST: distinct from قرب (generic spatial-or-temporal nearness); أزف is the marked term for URGENT, on-the-verge imminence of a fixed appointed moment — real discrimination, not a vague blob. Falsifiable via a clear failure condition (pure spatial nearness / emptied name / distress-without-imminence) that no occurrence meets. Caveat noted for transparency: dataset is small (only 2 verses, both eschatological, one word a proper-name epithet), but the verb+participle pairing in 53:57 gives internal arbitration strong enough to license SUPPORTED rather than PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED.
